newsitem.title: USA: Navistar says truck, engine markets strong. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Navistar says truck, engine markets strong. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Navistar International Corp said Thursday it expected strong demand in the truck and engine markets and raised its 1997 forecast for industry demand for heavy and medium trucks in the U.S. and Canada.
(Corrects to show Navistar raised its outlook for heavy trucks and medium trucks. The company did not drastically change its outlook for school buses.)

"We continue to see a strong truck and engine market, and we plan to raise production schedules in the fourth quarter to meet increased demand," John Horne, chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

The manufacturer said it planned to lift production at its Springfield, Ohio, truck assembly plant in early September on its medium truck and school bus line to 300 from 284 units per day, and heavy truck production will increase to 80 from 65.
Production will remain at 100 units per day at the Chatham, Ontario premium conventional heavy-truck assembly plant, Navistar said.

Engine production at its Indianapolis plant will rise to 933 from 830 units a day by the end of August. Efficiencies at the Engine & Foundry Group in man hours per engine and gains in uptime and first-time yield will help improve production.
Meanwhile Navistar raised its forecast for industry demand for heavy and medium trucks in the United States and Canada.

The company lifted its heavy truck forecast to 190,000 units in fiscal year 1997 from a previous forecast of 180,000 units that the company issued in May. Last year, the industry sold 195,400 heavy trucks.

Navistar increased its forecast for medium trucks in the United States and Canada to 114,000 units from its previous outlook of 112,000. The new forecast would represent a slight increase from the 113,200 trucks sold in 1996.

The company said it expected demand for school buses in fiscal 1997 to be 30,500 versus the 32,500 buses sold in 1996. The forecast did not mark a big change from previous expectations, said spokeswoman Rebecca Hayne.
Navistar earlier said it earned $35 million, or $0.38 a share, during the third quarter compared to $17 million, or $0.13 a share, in the same period last year.

Commenting on new product development, Horne said, "We are encouraged by positive customer response to both our Pro Sleeper Skyrise, which targets the long-haul customer, and the new International 9100 truck, which meets the needs of regional haulers."

To date, more than 3,100 of the International 9100 trucks have been ordered, it said. Navistar's total U.S. and Canadian Class 8 market share was up to 17.8 percent for the nine months versus 17.1 percent in the same period a year ago.
